newsitem.title: USA: GE signs new Hudson Falls cleanup agreement.
newsitem.headline: GE signs new Hudson Falls cleanup agreement.

text.p: The New York Department of Environmental Conservation said Thursday General Electric Co will continue the cleanup of its Hudson Falls, N.Y., plant site under a new agreement with the department.
A consent order signed by Commissioner John Cahill on July 7 replaces two 1993 consent orders relating to the cleanup of polychlorinated biphenyls (PCBs) at the site.
Under the agreement, DEC said, it will select final cleanup plans for the site after GE completes its investigation and evaluation of alternatives.

It said GE has agreed to reimburse the state's previous and future costs of overseeing work at the site. GE agreed to pay $256,517 to cover costs incurred before December 31, 1995, for studying and monitoring the clean up of PCBs released from the GE plant and adjacent areas.
The company also agreed to pay up to $200,000 for similar work conducted since January 1, 1996 and in the future.

The Hudson Falls site has been the focus of a major PCB cleanup since 1993, including removal of more than 120 tons of PCBs from the site. The effort has significantly reduced the amount of PCBs in Hudson River water immediately downstream of the GE Hudson Falls site, the department said.
GE manufactured electrical capacitors from 1952 to 1990 at the 17 acre site located on the eastern shore of the Hudson River in Washington County.
